chinese: 曲则全，枉则直，洼则盈，敝则新，少则得，多则惑。
是以圣人抱一为天下式。
不自见故明，不自是故彰，不自伐故有功，不自矜故长。
夫唯不争，故天下莫能与之争。
古之所谓曲则全者，岂虚言哉！
pinyin: Qū zé quán， wǎng zé zhí， wā zé yíng， bì zé xīn， shǎo zé dé， duō zé huò。
Shì yǐ shèng rén bào yī wèi tiān xià shì。
Bù zì jiàn gù míng， bù zì shì gù zhāng， bù zì fá gù yǒu gōng， bù zì jīn gù zhǎng。
Fū wéi bù zhēng， gù tiān xià mò néng yǔ zhī zhēng。
Gǔ zhī suǒ wèi qū zé quán zhě， qǐ xū yán zāi！
english: If you want to become whole, first let yourself become broken. If you want to become straight, first let yourself become twisted. If you want to become full, first let yourself become empty. If you want to become new, first let yourself become old. Those whose desires are few get them, those whose desires are great go astray.

For this reason the Master embraces the Tao, as an example for the world to follow. Because she isn't self centered, people can see the light in her. Because she does not boast of herself, she becomes a shining example. Because she does not glorify herself, she becomes a person of merit. Because she wants nothing from the world, the world can not overcome her.
When the ancient Masters said, "If you want to become whole, then first let yourself be broken," they weren't using empty words. All who do this will be made complete.
